factors.name: CEQA full EIR is a 12–24+ month critical path with high litigation exposure
factors.evidence: A 100 MW solar+storage project on farmland in CA requires a full EIR: 12–24 months to certify, 18–30 months total entitlement, +1–3 years if litigated. Renewables are the most-frequently-challenged project type (~43% plaintiff win rate vs EIRs). Farmland impact is scored via the Agricultural LESA Model and is likely 'significant and unavoidable,' requiring a Statement of Overriding Considerations. This alone can push any COD target out by 2–3+ years.

factors.name: OBBBA ITC beginning-of-construction cliff — deadline already passed
factors.evidence: Under OBBBA (July 2025) and IRS Notice 2025-42, a project with COD July 2028 receives $0 in solar ITC/PTC unless beginning-of-construction was documented by July 4, 2026 — a deadline that has already passed. No 5% safe harbor applies to >1.5 MW solar. Any permitting delay compounds this; the BOC evidence package is the single biggest go/no-go item. Storage ITC (§48E) survives the solar/wind cliff.

factors.name: Williamson Act land is an incompatible use — cancellation cost and schedule risk
factors.evidence: Commercial solar is an incompatible use on Williamson Act-contracted land. Exit paths: 9-year nonrenewal, or cancellation at 12.5% of unrestricted FMV (25% for Farmland Security Zone), or a solar-use easement at 6.25% (impaired farmland only). Ventura County has substantial agricultural/Williamson Act acreage; the parcel's contract status must be verified before entitlement. Cancellation adds cost and a discretionary county action that can be challenged.

factors.name: CEC Opt-In route eligibility and mandatory CBA/prevailing-wage conditions
factors.evidence: The CEC Opt-In Certification (AB 205/AB 209) is the only path that preempts local zoning, but eligibility requires solar ≥50 MW AND storage ≥200 MWh. The 100 MW solar qualifies on solar, but the storage must be ≥200 MWh or the project is ineligible. The certificate requires a certified community benefits agreement plus prevailing wage and skilled-and-trained workforce. If storage <200 MWh, the project falls back to the full local entitlement + CEQA EIR path.

findings.title: CEQA full EIR is a 12–24+ month critical path with high litigation exposure
findings.text: A 100 MW solar+storage project on farmland in CA requires a full EIR: 12–24 months to certify, 18–30 months total entitlement, +1–3 years if litigated. Renewables are the most-frequently-challenged project type (~43% plaintiff win rate vs EIRs). Farmland impact is scored via the Agricultural LESA Model and is likely 'significant and unavoidable,' requiring a Statement of Overriding Considerations. This alone can push any COD target out by 2–3+ years.

findings.title: OBBBA ITC beginning-of-construction cliff — deadline already passed
findings.text: Under OBBBA (July 2025) and IRS Notice 2025-42, a project with COD July 2028 receives $0 in solar ITC/PTC unless beginning-of-construction was documented by July 4, 2026 — a deadline that has already passed. No 5% safe harbor applies to >1.5 MW solar. Any permitting delay compounds this; the BOC evidence package is the single biggest go/no-go item. Storage ITC (§48E) survives the solar/wind cliff.

findings.title: Williamson Act land is an incompatible use — cancellation cost and schedule risk
findings.text: Commercial solar is an incompatible use on Williamson Act-contracted land. Exit paths: 9-year nonrenewal, or cancellation at 12.5% of unrestricted FMV (25% for Farmland Security Zone), or a solar-use easement at 6.25% (impaired farmland only). Ventura County has substantial agricultural/Williamson Act acreage; the parcel's contract status must be verified before entitlement. Cancellation adds cost and a discretionary county action that can be challenged.

findings.title: CEC Opt-In route eligibility and mandatory CBA/prevailing-wage conditions
findings.text: The CEC Opt-In Certification (AB 205/AB 209) is the only path that preempts local zoning, but eligibility requires solar ≥50 MW AND storage ≥200 MWh. The 100 MW solar qualifies on solar, but the storage must be ≥200 MWh or the project is ineligible. The certificate requires a certified community benefits agreement plus prevailing wage and skilled-and-trained workforce. If storage <200 MWh, the project falls back to the full local entitlement + CEQA EIR path.

findings.title: CAISO interconnection schedule compounds the permitting timeline
findings.text: Ventura is in CAISO/SCE territory. CAISO queue is >500 GW / ~1,000 projects; historically only ~20% of queued projects reach COD, and typical IR→COD is ~5 years. Network-upgrade cost shock is the #1 dropout driver. Any COD target must be reconciled against both the CEQA EIR timeline and the interconnection cluster study schedule.
